title: Compact model rollout lab diary — week of 2028-08-04
body:
Purpose: quick lab diary capturing the compact-model (4-bit/8-bit mixture) rollout experiments and evaluation signals observed this week. This is informal — notes, hypotheses, failures, and next steps. Goal for sprint: validate 4-bit + KV-cache compatibility for chat workloads and get a safe canary plan for Dedicated tier.

Summary of work completed (high level):
- Spun up three model variants for canary tests: base-fp16 (control), q4_ks8 (4-bit kernel-select), and q8_dynamic (8-bit mixed).
- Ran the baseline eval suite (1000 prompts from production-sampled prompt set) across the three variants with KV-cache enabled and disabled.
- Added instrumentation for per-token latency percentile (p50/p95/p99), KV cache hit rate, and per-response quality score (BLEU-like + semantic-sim via embed-sim).
- Preliminary traffic shaping: 5% canary traffic to q4_ks8 on an internal Dedicated pool (2xA10G equiv) for 24h.

Key observations (what surprised us):
- Latency: q4_ks8 p95 token latency reduced ~18% vs fp16 for median-length (128 tokens) sequences with KV-cache ON. p99 improvement inconsistent: in some tails q4_ks8 p99 was slightly worse (up to +12ms) when concurrent microbatching triggered. Suspect kernel scheduling contention in the runtime when mixed precision paths are active.
- Cost: token-cost-per-1000 reduced ~42% in q4_ks8 vs fp16 on the Dedicated pool (raw GPU-msecs -> cost mapping).
- Quality: aggregate semantic-sim score drop was tiny (~0.6% absolute) for q4_ks8 on general-purpose prompts, but for arithmetic/retrieval-augmented prompts we saw ~2.4% drop and some hallucination spikes on 1.8% of samples.
- KV-cache interaction: when KV-cache hit-rate was >65% for long-form chats, q4_ks8 maintained quality; but for turn-based short chats where hits were low, quantization effects amplified.
- Batch sizing: microbatch windowing of 12–20ms gave best throughput/latency tradeoff for q4_ks8. Above ~30ms we saw degraded p99 due to larger combined attention spans.

Experiments and results (quick log):
- EXP-2028-08-04-A: 1k-sample eval, KV-cache ON, q4_ks8 vs fp16. Result: quality delta -0.6% semantic-sim, latency p95 -18%. Note: hallucination log id range X-1200..X-1218 flagged for manual triage.
- EXP-2028-08-04-B: 1k-sample eval, KV-cache OFF, q4_ks8 vs fp16. Result: quality delta -1.9%, latency improvement smaller (-7%).
- EXP-2028-08-04-C: microburst throughput test (500 concurrent short chats), q4_ks8. Result: CPU-side lockups observed during kernel swap events (ticket: JIRA-ENG-7821).
- EXP-2028-08-04-D: q8_dynamic baseline for edge case prompts (math, time series). Result: quality within -0.4% vs fp16, latency gains ~9%. No kernel swap lockups.

Examples and representative failures: (copy of a few problematic prompts)
- Prompt A (retrieval augment): asked for step-by-step calculation reference; q4_ks8 produced confident but incorrect intermediate step; fp16 correct. Happens when retrieved context tokens > 1024 and cache segmentation crosses microbatch boundary.
- Prompt B (few-shot coding): q4_ks8 produced slightly truncated code block in ~1.1% responses; likely subtle EOS token scoring drift.

Hypotheses (why things happened):
1) Kernel scheduling edge-case: when kernel-selection switches between quantized and non-quantized paths mid-request (due to dynamic batching with mixed variants), serialization adds jitter and occasionally increases p99.
2) Quantization sensitivity depends on prompt shape: tasks requiring precise arithmetic or compositional reasoning are more affected; these are underrepresented in the generic eval set.
3) KV-cache fragmentation: for long chats that cross microbatch boundaries, the cache read path sometimes triggers dequant/rescale rounding that harms arithmetic stability.

Immediate actions taken:
- Rolled back canary from 5% -> 1% while triaging the kernel scheduling lockups.
- Added additional logging around kernel selection events and batch composition in the runtime (PR: serving-runtime/pull/1892).
- Expanded eval set with 2k targeted prompts for arithmetic, retrieval-augmented QA, and code synthesis (subset named: compact-rollout-focus-set).

Open questions / things to test next sprint: (prioritized)
- Q1: Can we avoid kernel-path switches mid-request by enforcing per-request kernel affinity? Cost/latency tradeoff? Owner: Diego.
- Q2: How much of the hallucination increase is due to quantization vs cache fragmentation? Need ablation: q4_ks8 + no-cache vs fp16 + simulated fragmentation. Owner: Aisha.
- Q3: Is there a quantization-aware calibration step for KV-cache rescaling that reduces arithmetic drift? Owner: Maya.
- Q4: For Dedicated customers with mixed model pools, what's a safe canary policy that doesn't induce mixed-kernel scheduling? Proposal: route a request atomically to a single variant or pin by route. Need product input. Owner: Liam -> sync w/ product-hosted-api.

Operational checklist (short):
- Alerts: p99 latency spike threshold for q4_ks8 set to +20ms over fp16 baseline. Slack alert channel: #applied-ml-ops.
- Dashboards: added kv-cache-hit vs quality scatter to compact rollout console dashboard.
- Canary policy: reduced to 1%, staggered ramp plan documented on confluence (link above).

Action items (assignments):
- Maya: implement KV-cache rescale ablation + run targeted evals (due 2028-08-10).
- Diego: prototype per-request kernel affinity flag in serving-runtime (draft PR by 2028-08-09).
- Aisha: curate 2000-sample focused eval set and run overnight batch (results on 2028-08-06).
- Liam: align with product on safe canary gating criteria for Dedicated customers (sync meeting 2028-08-07).
- Sana: triage and annotate hallucination cases for developer review (spreadsheet link in confluence page).

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep an eye on microbatch window tuning — small wins are easy but tail behavior is the tricky bit.
- Consider a short doc for customer-facing guidance: "What to expect with compact quantized variants" — include recommended workloads and known limitations. Might be useful for solutions-engineering.

Meeting summary (standup 2028-08-05):
- Quick sync: canary reduced, kernel lockups prioritized.
- Diego showed trace where two kernel contexts were scheduled for same GPU stream -> spike correlation.
- Aisha presented preliminary histogram of semantic-sim by task type; arithmetic and retrieval clearly lower.
- Action owners reiterated above.

Appendix (short logs and commands used):
- eval-runner command: ./eval-runner --suite compact-rollout-focus-set --variant q4_ks8 --kv-cache on --out results/q4_kv_on_20280804.csv
- trace sample: gpu-trace-20280804-03.log (uploaded to S3 /internal/traces/).

If you read nothing else: q4_ks8 gives large cost and median-latency wins, but we need to address kernel scheduling and a small cluster of hallucination/regression signals on arithmetic/retrieval prompts before broad rollout.

End of diary entry.

-- Maya
